title: Failover, Switchover & Split-Brain Prevention
description: Understand planned switchovers, unplanned disaster failover, and quorum consensus to prevent Split-Brain scenarios.

data.text: In database clustering, **Switchover** is a controlled, planned promotion of a replica to primary (e.g. for maintenance). **Failover** is an emergency, automated promotion when the primary node crashes.

A **Split-Brain** occurs when a network partition disconnects nodes, causing both the old primary and the promoted replica to believe they are the authoritative primary. Both accept conflicting writes, causing irreversible data divergence. High-availability clusters prevent this using distributed consensus engines (etcd, Consul, Raft) with odd-numbered quorums (3 or 5 nodes).

A switchover is a controlled failover: you demote the current primary, let the replica catch up, and promote the replica. The goal is to do it with no data loss and minimal downtime. In a managed cluster this is one command; by hand, the sequence is to stop writes, wait for the replica to be fully caught up, promote it, and repoint the application.

data.title: Manual switchover sequence
data.content: Catch-up is confirmed by comparing WAL positions, so promotion happens only after zero lag.

data.title: Interview angle: split-brain is the failure you design against
data.text: The dangerous scenario is a network partition where the replica is promoted while the old primary still thinks it is primary, so two nodes accept writes and diverge. No single PostgreSQL server can prevent that alone. Production clusters use a distributed consensus store (etcd or Consul via Patroni, or a witness in repmgr) so only a node with a quorum-granted leader lease can act as primary. Fencing the old primary — shutting it down or revoking its storage — is the second half of the answer.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Switchovers are planned and safe; failovers are automated responses to disasters.
Prevent split-brain by requiring quorum consensus (3+ nodes) via etcd or Consul.
Fence old primaries using STONITH (Shoot The Other Node In The Head) or node termination.
